title: ÆTHER: Midnight City (modern founder drama main theme)
story: A young founder in a modern Indian city has one night to save her startup; lonely 2 AM restlessness turns into confident triumph at sunrise.
script:
# Midnight City: outline (written before the music)

**Genre:** modern city drama, the main theme of a young founder's story. About 90 s.
**Story:** 2 AM in Bengaluru. A young woman's startup is failing, her team has gone home, and she has one night before the investors meet. She rides the empty metro, finds the idea, builds it all night, and walks into the launch at sunrise.
**Feeling:** lonely, restless night that turns into confident, modern triumph.

| Time | Scene | Music |
|---|---|---|
| 0-8 s | Empty glass office at 2 AM, one laptop glowing, city lights outside. | A soft synth pulse and the 3-note call on a clean electric piano. |
| 8-20 s | She shuts the laptop and walks out into the neon street. | Soft female humming sings the main melody over a deep 808 hum. |
| 20-34 s | The empty night metro; rain streaks the window; she watches the city go by. | A half-time beat with trap hi-hats and a light tabla; the bansuri answers the humming. |
| 34-46 s | A spark: she sees the idea in the city lights and starts typing on the train. | A synth arpeggio speeds up, a reversed swell, the melody climbs. |
| 46-70 s | All-night building montage: code, coffee, whiteboards, the sky turning blue. | The full drop: the same melody on a bright synth lead, humming and electric guitar together, punchy drums and 808 bass. |
| 70-82 s | Sunrise. She walks into the pitch room and the screen lights up. | The melody comes back a step higher, the biggest moment. |
| 82-90 s | She smiles at the city from the window. | The beat drops away, the humming sings the first phrase once more, the call on electric piano ends it. |

**Raga:** Charukesi in D (bright start, then the flat sixth gives the ache), played with today's sounds. One melody all the way through, one continuous generation.

brief.notes: Jithesh 30 Oct 11:21 on The Long Way Home outline: 'Why are you stuck on this kingdom? Come out of that one. We are in the modern world, so music should be for modern people and concept.' Replaces long-way-home (village story). Outline only (11:18). Modern palette (808, trap hats, synths, e-guitar) with Indian writing, Charukesi in D, humming voice, natural bansuri/tabla, Broken Heritage layer, one continuous generation. Prompt mode, music_v2.

prompt: ONE single modern cinematic main theme for a young founder's story in a big modern Indian city at night: lonely and restless at 2 AM, ending in confident triumph at sunrise. Today's sound, glossy, fresh and modern: deep 808 sub bass, punchy half-time drums with crisp trap hi-hats, analog synth arpeggios, a bright synth lead, clean electric piano, electric guitar, wide modern mix. Written the way today's South Indian film composers write: the whole track is built on ONE memorable melody that returns again and again; nothing unrelated is introduced, it grows only through sound and energy, one continuous story. Raga Charukesi (a Mixolydian flat-six scale) in D: D E F# G A Bb C. The melody starts bright on D E F# G, then leans on the flat sixth Bb and falls Bb A G F# with an ache; rising phrases climb A Bb C D. Sung-style phrasing with gamakam: slides into notes, a shake on F# and Bb, grace notes, the synth lead bends like a voice. Modal on a D pedal, few chord changes, no Western pop chord loop. The voice: a soft, close, natural wordless female humming voice (mm and aa) carries the melody. Real bansuri flute and a light tabla, played by real musicians, close, dry and natural, no heavy echo, not chopped. A separate electronic layer: a chopped glitching veena answering phrases, a pitched-down mridangam as an extra low hit, a reversed veena swell before the drop. One steady tempo, 88 BPM half-time feel, never stopping. 0-8 s: only a soft synth pulse and a clean electric piano playing a rising 3-note call D F A with the last note bent up, 2 AM in an empty glass office. 8-20 s: the female humming sings the melody softly over a deep 808 hum. 20-34 s: the half-time beat starts with trap hi-hats and a light tabla, rain and the night metro; the bansuri answers each humming phrase. 34-46 s: a synth arpeggio speeds up, the melody climbs, a reversed veena swell, the spark of an idea. 46-70 s: the full drop: the same melody on a bright synth lead with the humming and electric guitar, punchy drums and 808 bass, driving and confident. 70-82 s: the melody returns a whole step higher in E, the biggest moment, sunrise. 82-90 s: the beat drops away, the humming sings the first phrase once more, the electric piano ends on the 3-note call. Modern and urban, not old-fashioned, not a period film, no village or temple sounds, not a royal or hero march, no orchestral trailer drums, no silences, no gaps, no heavy echo on the flute or voice, no lyrics.
